_meta.indication: LUNSUMIO is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma after two or more lines of systemic therapy; approved under accelerated approval based on response rate.

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase I/II first-in-human dose escalation and expansion study
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma who had received at least two prior therapies, including an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody and an alkylating agent
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Objective response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR) assessed by an independent review facility

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) were cytokine release syndrome (39%), fatigue (36%), rash (34%), pyrexia (24%), and headache (21%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 47% of patients. CRS occurred in 39% of patients (Grade 3 in 2%, Grade 4 in 0.5%).
target_moa: Bispecific CD20-directed CD3 T-cell engager; a humanized IgG1 anti-CD20xCD3 bispecific antibody that promotes T-cell dependent killing of B-cells through CD20 (on B-cells) and CD3 (on T-cells).
modality: bispecific (humanized IgG1 anti-CD20xCD3 T-cell-dependent bispecific antibody)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: CYTOKINE RELEASE SYNDROME — CRS, including serious or life-threatening reactions, can occur; initiate treatment with the step-up dosing schedule to reduce risk; withhold or permanently discontinue based on severity.

rems.type: The Division of Risk Management concurred that additional REMS are not required for the safe use of mosunetuzumab in the indicated population.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not presented to the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee because it did not raise significant efficacy or safety issues for the recommended indication.

description.text: Safety labeling update: added Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis warning and expanded neurologic toxicity/ICANS data; no new indication or population added

citations.quote: - Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis: Added to Warnings and Precautions (Section 5.4)

description.text: Added a new subcutaneous route of administration (Lunsumio Velo) for adults with relapsed/refractory follicular lymphoma after two or more lines of systemic therapy

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for a new subcutaneous (SC) route of administration of mosunetuzumab-axgb for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma after two or more lines of systemic therapy.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Response rate (ORR/complete response rate); CR rate was chosen as the primary endpoint and is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit in FL.

citations.quote: This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on response rate [see *Clinical Studies* (14.1)]. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial(s).

CR rate was chosen as the primary endpoint as it is clinically relevant, directly attributable to drug effect and not the natural history of the disease, is based on objective and quantitative assessments, and appropriate for a single arm study. Several lines of evidence indicate that CR rate is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit in patients with FL to support accelerated approval. The

confirmatory_requirement.text: PMR 4375-1: a randomized trial in relapsed/refractory FL comparing mosunetuzumab plus lenalidomide vs rituximab plus lenalidomide, with primary endpoint of progression-free survival, to verify and describe clinical benefit.

citations.quote: 4375-1 Conduct a randomized clinical trial in patients with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma, with patients randomized to receive mosunetuzumab in combination with lenalidomide or rituximab in combination with lenalidomide. The primary endpoint should be progression-free survival, with secondary endpoints that include response rate and overall survival. The trial should enroll a sufficiently representative study population to reflect the racial and ethnic diversity of the U.S. patient population with follicular lymphoma and allow for interpretation of the results in these patient populations.

summary.text: Lunsumio received accelerated approval based on response rate under a Priority review BLA, supported by Breakthrough Therapy Designation (June 2020) and Orphan Drug Designation (December 2018), with a confirmatory randomized trial required as a postmarketing requirement to verify clinical benefit.

citations.quote: The FDA review team recommends accelerated approval of mosunetuzumab for the following indication:
2 June 2020	Breakthrough Therapy Designation was granted for the treatment of adult patients with R/R FL who have received at least two prior systemic therapies
17 December 2018	Orphan Drug Designation was granted for treatment of FL

Products approved under the accelerated approval regulations, 21 CFR 601.41, require further adequate and well-controlled clinical trials to verify and describe clinical benefit. You are required to conduct such clinical trials with due diligence. If postmarketing clinical trials fail to verify clinical benefit or are not conducted with due diligence, we may, following a hearing in accordance with 21 CFR 601.43(b), withdraw this approval. We remind you of your postmarketing requirement specified in your submission dated November 22, 2022. This requirement, along with required completion dates, is listed below.

requirement.text: 4375-1: Conduct a randomized clinical trial in patients with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma, randomizing to mosunetuzumab plus lenalidomide or rituximab plus lenalidomide, with primary endpoint of progression-free survival (secondary endpoints response rate and overall survival).

citations.quote: 4375-1 Conduct a randomized clinical trial in patients with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma, with patients randomized to receive mosunetuzumab in combination with lenalidomide or rituximab in combination with lenalidomide. The primary endpoint should be progression-free survival, with secondary endpoints that include response rate and overall survival. The trial should enroll a sufficiently representative study population to reflect the racial and ethnic diversity of the U.S. patient population with follicular lymphoma and allow for interpretation of the results in these patient populations.

requirement.text: 4375-2: Conduct an integrated safety analysis in patients with follicular lymphoma and other lymphoid malignancies to further characterize the incidence and severity of neurologic adverse reactions, hematologic adverse reactions, hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, infections, and pneumonitis/interstitial lung disease with longer term use of mosunetuzumab.

citations.quote: 4375-2 Conduct an integrated safety analysis in patients with follicular lymphoma and other lymphoid malignancies to further characterize the incidence and severity of neurologic adverse reactions, hematologic adverse reactions, hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, infections, and pneumonitis/interstitial lung disease, that may develop with longer term use of mosunetuzumab.
